gen.title: Comparing index populations for escalation agreements

values.value: over 90 percent of the total U.S. population
values.quote: The CPI-U represents over 90 percent of the total U.S. population and is based on the expenditures of all families living in urban areas.
Because the CPI-U population coverage is more comprehensive, it is used in most other escalation agreements.

values.value: approximately 30 percent of the total U.S. population
values.quote: The CPI-W represents approximately 30 percent of the total U.S. population.
The CPI-W is used for escalation primarily in blue-collar cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs).

checks.message: every compare-table text length is within the frozen limits and every row and column name uses page words, never an id
all 4 cell quote(s) appear verbatim in their cited source after whitespace normalisation (quotes-verbatim)

every cell value occurs in its quote and every row entity occurs in the quote or the same source paragraph (cell-in-quote; paragraph-level entity attribution is the design-disclosed false accept — quotes are visible)
the table shape is valid: 2 rows x 2 attributes with exactly one value per row-column slot (shape-valid)
every number in entity names, attributes and cell values appears on the cited page or in the same quote (N-01) (numbers-checkable)

no attribute column offers 3 distinct cell values, so the UI falls back to reveal-only with unverified cells blanked as "Not stated on this page" — by design this is not a component failure (predict-cell-valid)
